14	/-!
15	# Unconditional higher direct images via Čech complexes, and flat base change
16	
17	For a separated quasi-compact morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S`, a finite affine open cover
18	`𝒰` of `X` and a quasi-coherent `F : X.Modules`, the higher direct image `Rⁱ f_* F` is the
19	`i`-th cohomology of the relative Čech complex `Č•(𝒰, F)`.  No enough-injectives hypothesis
20	on `O_X`-modules is needed: it is the cohomology of an explicit complex of quasi-coherent
21	sheaves.  The bulk of the file establishes flat base change for these Čech higher direct
22	images: for a cartesian square with `g : S' ⟶ S` flat, `g^*(Rⁱ f_* F) ≅ Rⁱ f'_* (g'^* F)`.
23	
24	The base-change proof reduces, through the product decomposition of a fibre power of the
25	cover into its intersection opens, to a Beck–Chevalley comparison over a single Čech
26	intersection open `U_σ`.  Over an affine base and for a separated `f` that open is affine,
27	the restricted cartesian square becomes a pushout square of rings, and the comparison is the
28	affine termwise base change of `FlatBaseChange.lean`, matched to the abstract push–pull
29	objects through the `tilde` dictionary over `Spec`.
30	
31	## Main results
32	
33	* `cechHigherDirectImage`: the `i`-th higher direct image, as the `i`-th cohomology of the
34	  relative Čech complex.
35	* `openImmersion_beckChevalley`: for a cartesian square base-changing an open immersion `p`
36	  onto an affine open along `g'`, the isomorphism `g'^*(p_* p^* F) ≅ p'_* p'^*(g'^* F)`.
37	* `pushPullObj_coverInter_baseChange`: base change of the push–pull object over a single Čech
38	  intersection open, over affine bases.
39	* `cechComplex_baseChange_iso`: applying `g^*` degreewise to `Č•(𝒰, F)` gives `Č•(𝒰', g'^* F)`
40	  for the base-changed cover `𝒰'` and the base-changed sheaf `g'^* F`.
41	* `cech_flatBaseChange`: flat base change for the Čech higher direct images.
42	
43	## Obligations not yet discharged
44	
45	Three statements below are still assumed rather than proved.
46	
47	* `pullback_preservesFiniteLimits`: for `g` flat, `g^*` preserves finite limits.  What is
48	  missing is left-exactness of the presheaf-level pullback; see the docstring there.
49	* the cosimplicial naturality of `cech_pushforward_baseChange_natIso` and of
50	  `twisted_cech_nerve_iso`.  In both cases the degreewise isomorphisms are constructed, and
51	  what remains is their compatibility with the index-omission maps generating the
52	  cosimplicial structure of the Čech nerve.
53	
54	Everything downstream of these — in particular `cechComplex_baseChange_iso` and
55	`cech_flatBaseChange` — is proved modulo them.
56	
57	## References
58	
59	* Stacks project, tags 02KG and 02KH (flat base change for cohomology), 01I8 (quasi-coherent
60	  sheaves on an affine scheme), 01BG (stability of quasi-coherence under pullback).
61	-/

71	variable {S S' X X' : Scheme.{u}}
72	
73	/-- **Unconditional higher direct image via Čech.** For a separated quasi-compact
74	`f : X ⟶ S`, a finite affine open cover `𝒰` of `X`, and a quasi-coherent
75	`F : X.Modules`, the `i`-th higher direct image is the `i`-th cohomology of the
76	relative Čech complex. This needs **no** enough-injectives hypothesis on
77	`O_X`-modules: it is the cohomology of an explicit complex of quasi-coherent
78	sheaves. By `cech_computes_higherDirectImage` it agrees with the derived-functor
79	higher direct image wherever the latter is defined, and is independent of the
80	chosen affine cover up to canonical isomorphism. For `i = 0` one recovers the
81	ordinary pushforward `R⁰ f_* F = f_* F`. -/
82	noncomputable def cechHigherDirectImage (f : X ⟶ S) (𝒰 : X.OpenCover)
83	    (F : X.Modules) (i : ℕ) : S.Modules :=
84	  (CechComplex f 𝒰 F).homology i
85	
86	/-! ### Structure of the proof of `cech_flatBaseChange` (Stacks 02KH, separated case)
87	
88	The proof decomposes into two independent halves, assembled in `cech_flatBaseChange`.
89	
90	1. **Homology side.** The pullback `g^*` is exact, so it commutes with
91	   `HomologicalComplex.homology`:
92	   * `pullback_preservesFiniteColimits` — `g^*` is a left adjoint;
93	   * `pullback_preservesFiniteLimits` — `g` flat implies `g^*` left-exact.  Mathlib has this
94	     affine-locally for extension of scalars,
95	     `ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat`, but not lifted through
96	     sheafification to `SheafOfModules.pullback`; this step is not yet proved;
97	   * `pullback_preservesHomology` — derived from the two previous items via
98	     `Functor.preservesHomologyOfExact`;
99	   * `mapHomologicalComplexHomologyIso` and `pullback_mapHC_homologyIso` — the complex-level
100	     form of `ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso`.
101	2. **`cechComplex_baseChange_iso` (Stacks 02KG).** Applying `g^*` degreewise to `Č•(𝒰, F)`
102	   recovers `Č•(𝒰', g'^* F)`.  It comes from `cechComplex_baseChange_cosimplicialIso`, the
103	   whiskered composite of the cosimplicial Beck–Chevalley isomorphism
104	   `cech_pushforward_baseChange_natIso` (degreewise the per-σ
105	   `pushPullObj_coverInter_baseChange`, routed through the bridge
106	   `pushPullObj_pushforward_iso_tilde` to the affine termwise base change
107	   `affinePushforwardPullbackBaseChange` over the ring pushout carved out by
108	   `restrictedCartesianAffinePushout`) with the twisted-nerve identification
109	   `twisted_cech_nerve_iso` (degreewise `twisted_cech_nerve_per_sigma`, itself the X-level
110	   open-immersion Beck–Chevalley `openImmersion_beckChevalley` over the cover-base-change
111	   identity `coverInterOpen_baseChange_eq`).  Both cosimplicial isomorphisms are constructed
112	   degreewise; their cosimplicial naturality is not yet proved.
113	
114	No spectral sequence is needed here: this is the *separated* case (`[IsSeparated f]`).
115	The Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence enters only in the promotion from the separated to
116	the general quasi-separated case of Stacks 02KH, which is not this statement. -/
117	
118	section HomologyComm
119	
120	variable {C D : Type*} [Category.{u} C] [Category.{u} D] [Preadditive C] [Preadditive D]
121	  [CategoryWithHomology C] [CategoryWithHomology D]
122	
123	/-- **Complex-level upgrade of `ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso`.** An additive functor `F`
124	that preserves homology commutes with `HomologicalComplex.homology`. The degree-`i`
125	short complex of `(F.mapHomologicalComplex c).obj K` is *definitionally* `F` applied to
126	the degree-`i` short complex `K.sc i` of `K` (both have `Xⱼ = F.obj (K.Xⱼ)` and
127	`d = F.map (K.d)`), so this is exactly `ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso (K.sc i) F`. -/
128	noncomputable def mapHomologicalComplexHomologyIso (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive]
129	    [F.PreservesHomology] {ι : Type*} {c : ComplexShape ι} (K : HomologicalComplex C c) (i : ι) :
130	    ((F.mapHomologicalComplex c).obj K).homology i ≅ F.obj (K.homology i) :=
131	  ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso (K.sc i) F
132	
133	end HomologyComm
134	
135	/-! ### Right exact + mono-preserving ⟹ left exact
136	
137	The categorical step that converts the flat-pullback obligation from a statement about
138	*all* finite limits into a statement about *monomorphisms only*.  For an additive functor
139	between abelian categories, right exactness (which `g^*` has for free, being a left
140	adjoint) plus preservation of monomorphisms already forces left exactness.  Indeed
141	`Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_iff_forall_exact_map_and_mono` says left exactness is
142	equivalent to: every short exact `0 → A → B → C → 0` maps to an exact `F A → F B → F C`
143	with `F A → F B` mono.  The exactness half is `ShortComplex.Exact.map_of_epi_of_preservesCokernel`
144	(available from right exactness alone, since `B → C` is epi), and the mono half is the
145	hypothesis.  Note this is *not* a "right exact ⟹ exact" fallacy: the mono hypothesis is
146	exactly the flatness input, and without it the statement is false (tensoring by a
147	non-flat module is right exact and not left exact). -/
148	section RightExactMono
149	
150	variable {C D : Type*} [Category.{u} C] [Category.{u} D] [Abelian C] [Abelian D]
151	
152	/-- **Right exact + mono-preserving ⟹ left exact**, for an additive functor between abelian
153	categories.  Project-local categorical supplement: mathlib has the TFAE
154	`Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_tfae` characterising left exactness by "short exact sequences
155	map to left-exact ones", and the right-exactness transport
156	`ShortComplex.Exact.map_of_epi_of_preservesCokernel`, but not this packaged criterion.
157	It is what reduces `pullback_preservesFiniteLimits` to mono-preservation. -/
158	theorem preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesMonomorphisms (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive]
159	    [Limits.PreservesFiniteColimits F] [F.PreservesMonomorphisms] :
160	    Limits.PreservesFiniteLimits F := by
161	  rw [F.preservesFiniteLimits_iff_forall_exact_map_and_mono]
162	  intro T hT
163	  have := hT.mono_f
164	  exact ⟨hT.exact.map_of_epi_of_preservesCokernel F hT.epi_g inferInstance, inferInstance⟩
165	
166	end RightExactMono
167	
168	/-! ### Monomorphisms of `𝒪_X`-modules are sectionwise
169	
170	The mono half of flat left-exactness is checked on sections, so both directions of
171	"mono ⟺ injective on sections" are needed.  The `⟸` direction (over a basis) is
172	`Modules.mono_of_injective_app_of_isBasis` in `Picard/FlatKernelBase.lean`; the `⟹`
173	direction is below.  Together they make mono-preservation of a *sectionwise* functor
174	mechanical, which discharges the open-immersion case of `pullback_preservesMonomorphisms`
175	outright. -/
176	
177	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
178	/-- **A monomorphism of `𝒪_X`-modules is injective on sections over every open.**  The
179	forgetful functor `Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf` preserves limits, hence monomorphisms; a
180	monomorphism of `Ab`-valued presheaves is one sectionwise (evaluation preserves limits);
181	and mono in `Ab` is injectivity.  Converse of `Modules.mono_of_injective_app_of_isBasis`
182	(`Picard/FlatKernelBase.lean`).  Project-local: mathlib has the iso-level
183	`Scheme.Modules.Hom.isIso_iff_isIso_app` but not the mono-level statement. -/
184	theorem Modules.injective_app_of_mono {X : Scheme.{u}} {M N : X.Modules} (φ : M ⟶ N)
185	    [Mono φ] (U : X.Opens) : Function.Injective (φ.app U) := by
186	  have h1 : Mono ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).map φ) := inferInstance
187	  haveI := h1
188	  have h2 : Mono (((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).map φ).app (Opposite.op U)) := inferInstance
189	  exact (AddCommGrpCat.mono_iff_injective _).mp h2
190	
191	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
192	/-- **Sectionwise criterion for a monomorphism of `𝒪_X`-modules.**  If `φ` is injective on
193	sections over *every* open then `φ` is a monomorphism: injectivity on all opens makes the
194	underlying `Ab`-presheaf morphism sectionwise mono, hence mono in the functor category, and
195	the faithful `Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf` reflects monomorphisms.  Converse of
196	`Modules.injective_app_of_mono`; a basis-local sharpening (only basic opens needed) is
197	`Modules.mono_of_injective_app_of_isBasis` in `Picard/FlatKernelBase.lean`, which this file
198	does not import.  Project-local. -/
199	theorem Modules.mono_of_injective_app {X : Scheme.{u}} {M N : X.Modules} {φ : M ⟶ N}
200	    (h : ∀ U : X.Opens, Function.Injective (φ.app U)) : Mono φ := by
201	  have hpre : Mono ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).map φ) := by
202	    haveI : ∀ U, Mono (((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).map φ).app U) := fun U =>
203	      (AddCommGrpCat.mono_iff_injective _).mpr (h U.unop)
204	    exact NatTrans.mono_of_mono_app _
205	  haveI := hpre
206	  exact (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).mono_of_mono_map hpre
207	
208	/-- **Restriction along an open immersion preserves monomorphisms.**  Restriction is
209	*sectionwise* — `((restrictFunctor f).map φ).app U = φ.app (f ''ᵁ U)` holds by `rfl`
210	(`Scheme.Modules.restrict_obj`) — so injectivity on sections transfers verbatim, and
211	`Modules.mono_of_injective_app_of_isBasis` over the basis of *all* opens concludes.
212	Combined with `Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback` this gives the open-immersion
213	case of `pullback_preservesMonomorphisms` with no flatness input beyond the (automatic)
214	flatness of an open immersion.  Project-local. -/
215	theorem Modules.restrictFunctor_preservesMonomorphisms {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
216	    [IsOpenImmersion f] : (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor f).PreservesMonomorphisms where
217	  preserves {M N} φ hφ := by
218	    haveI := hφ
219	    refine Modules.mono_of_injective_app (fun U => ?_)
220	    exact Modules.injective_app_of_mono φ (f ''ᵁ U)
221	
222	/-- **Flat pullback along an open immersion preserves monomorphisms** — the open-immersion
223	case of `pullback_preservesMonomorphisms`, transported from
224	`Modules.restrictFunctor_preservesMonomorphisms` along
225	`Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback`.  Project-local. -/
226	theorem Modules.pullback_preservesMonomorphisms_of_isOpenImmersion {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
227	    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion f] :
228	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).PreservesMonomorphisms :=
229	  haveI := Modules.restrictFunctor_preservesMonomorphisms f
230	  Functor.preservesMonomorphisms.of_iso (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback f)
231	
232	/-- **Flat base change has left-adjoint pullback**, hence `g^*` preserves finite
233	colimits (free: `g^* = pullback g` is a left adjoint). -/
234	instance pullback_preservesFiniteColimits (g : S' ⟶ S) :
235	    Limits.PreservesFiniteColimits (Scheme.Modules.pullback g) := inferInstance
236	
237	/-- **Reduction of flat left-exactness to mono-preservation.**  For any `g`, if the module
238	pullback `g^*` preserves monomorphisms then it preserves finite limits: it is additive and
239	right exact (a left adjoint), so `preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesMonomorphisms` applies.
240	This is the *whole* categorical content of `pullback_preservesFiniteLimits`; the residual
241	mathematics is the single statement `Mono (g^* ι)` for a mono `ι`, i.e. that flat pullback
242	does not destroy injections (Stacks 00HL / 01BG stalkwise).  Project-local. -/
243	theorem pullback_preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesMonomorphisms (g : S' ⟶ S)
244	    (h : (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).PreservesMonomorphisms) :
245	    Limits.PreservesFiniteLimits (Scheme.Modules.pullback g) :=
246	  haveI := h
247	  preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesMonomorphisms (Scheme.Modules.pullback g)
248	
249	/-- **Flat pullback preserves monomorphisms** (OPEN — the sole residual content of flat
250	left-exactness, after `pullback_preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesMonomorphisms`).
251	
252	The statement is true for *arbitrary* `𝒪_S`-modules, not just quasi-coherent ones, and the
253	only proof is stalkwise: for `x : S'` the stalk of `g^* M` is
254	`M_{g(x)} ⊗_{𝒪_{S,g(x)}} 𝒪_{S',x}`, the stalk map `𝒪_{S,g(x)} ⟶ 𝒪_{S',x}` of a flat `g` is
255	flat (`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.iff_flat_stalkMap`), and a flat base change preserves
256	injections; mono in `S'.Modules` is then detected on stalks
257	(`TopCat.Presheaf.mono_of_stalk_mono` through the faithful `Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf`, as in
258	`Modules.mono_of_injective_app_of_isBasis`).
259	
260	**Why this is not discharged here, stated precisely so the next session does not re-derive
261	the dead ends.**  Mathlib defines `SheafOfModules.pullback` as `(pushforward φ).leftAdjoint`
262	and gives it *no* pointwise description; `SheafOfModules.pullbackIso` factors it as
263	`forget ⋙ PresheafOfModules.pullback φ.hom ⋙ PresheafOfModules.sheafification`, whose outer
264	two factors are left exact in mathlib already (`SheafOfModules.Finite.forgetPreservesFiniteLimits`
265	and the `PreservesFiniteLimits (sheafification α)` instance, both of which *do* synthesise on
266	the scheme site — checked), but whose middle factor `PresheafOfModules.pullback` is again
267	only a left adjoint with no formula.  So the missing input is the same either way: a stalk (or
268	affine-section) model of the module pullback.
269	
270	Two routes that do **not** work, and why:
271	* the *affine* section formula `Scheme.Modules.pullback_app_isoTensor` (Picard/QuotScheme.lean)
272	  does give `Γ(g^* N, U) ≅ Γ(N, V) ⊗_{Γ(S,V)} Γ(S',U)` and would combine with
273	  `Modules.mono_of_injective_app_of_isBasis` — but it carries `[N.IsQuasicoherent]`, which the
274	  instance's statement (all modules) does not, and over an affine base `Scheme.Modules` is
275	  *not* `ModuleCat Γ(S,⊤)`, so quasi-coherence cannot be dropped from that route;
276	* there is no mathlib "right exact + preserves monos ⟹ exact" gap any more — that is closed
277	  above by `preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesMonomorphisms` — so the categorical glue is
278	  *not* what is missing.  The whole obligation is now this one mono statement.
279	
280	**What IS discharged**: the *open-immersion* case, sorry-free, as
281	`Modules.pullback_preservesMonomorphisms_of_isOpenImmersion` above — because there `g^*` is
282	isomorphic to the sectionwise `restrictFunctor`.
283	So the residual is genuinely about a general flat `g`, where no sectionwise formula holds and
284	the stalk model is unavoidable. -/
285	theorem pullback_preservesMonomorphisms (g : S' ⟶ S) [Flat g] :
286	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).PreservesMonomorphisms := sorry
287	
288	/-- **Flat implies `g^*` is left-exact.**  Now a two-line derivation: `g^*` is additive and
289	right exact (a left adjoint, `pullback_preservesFiniteColimits`), so by
290	`pullback_preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesMonomorphisms` left exactness follows from
291	mono-preservation, which for a flat `g` is `pullback_preservesMonomorphisms`.
292	
293	**DELIBERATELY NOT AN `instance`.**  It was one until this revision, and that was the worse
294	choice: as an instance it was picked up by typeclass synthesis at arbitrary sites, so any
295	declaration *quantifying over* it reported clean axioms while every *synthesis site* silently
296	acquired `sorryAx` — the leak the AJC ledger warns about.  As a plain theorem the dependency is
297	visible in every proof term that uses it (`haveI := pullback_preservesFiniteLimits g` below),
298	and no declaration acquires `sorryAx` without naming it.  Do **not** restore the `instance`
299	attribute before `pullback_preservesMonomorphisms` is proved; once it is, the attribute is free
300	and harmless.
301	
302	The leak now has a single named carrier, `pullback_preservesMonomorphisms`, whose statement is
303	one line of mathematics (flat base change preserves injections, stalkwise) rather than a
304	three-functor sheafification argument.  Measure at a synthesis site, e.g.
305	`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`'s `leakProbe_pullback_finiteLimits`. -/
306	theorem pullback_preservesFiniteLimits (g : S' ⟶ S) [Flat g] :
307	    Limits.PreservesFiniteLimits (Scheme.Modules.pullback g) :=
308	  pullback_preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesMonomorphisms g
309	    (pullback_preservesMonomorphisms g)
310	
311	/-- **Flat implies `g^*` preserves homology**, derived from left-exactness together with
312	left-adjointness via `Functor.preservesHomologyOfExact`.  Not an `instance`, for the same
313	reason as `pullback_preservesFiniteLimits`: its only unproved input is
314	`pullback_preservesMonomorphisms`, and that dependency should be visible rather than
315	synthesised. -/
316	theorem pullback_preservesHomology (g : S' ⟶ S) [Flat g] :
317	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).PreservesHomology :=
318	  haveI := pullback_preservesFiniteLimits g
319	  Functor.preservesHomologyOfExact _
320	
321	/-- **`g^*` commutes with Čech homology** (flat exactness, at the level of complexes).
322	A specialisation of `mapHomologicalComplexHomologyIso` to `g^* = pullback g`, which is
323	additive and, for `g` flat, preserves homology. -/
324	noncomputable def pullback_mapHC_homologyIso (g : S' ⟶ S) [Flat g]
325	    (K : CochainComplex S.Modules ℕ) (i : ℕ) :
326	    (((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj K).homology i
327	      ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj (K.homology i) :=
328	  haveI := pullback_preservesHomology g
329	  mapHomologicalComplexHomologyIso (Scheme.Modules.pullback g) K i

Let `M` be a presheaf of `R`-modules on a topological space. We endow `M.presheaf.stalk x` with
an `R.stalk x`-module structure.

The key characterizing lemma is `PresheafOfModules.germ_smul`, which describes the compatibility

namespace CategoryTheory.Limits

/-- (Implementation). The scalar multiplication function on `ColimitType`. -/
protected noncomputable
def colimit.smul (r : (R ⋙ forget _).ColimitType) (m : (M ⋙ forget _).ColimitType) :
    (M ⋙ forget _).ColimitType := by
  refine Quot.liftOn₂ r m (fun Ua Vb ↦ Functor.ιColimitType _ (max Ua.1 Vb.1) <|
    letI a : R.obj (max Ua.1 Vb.1) := R.map (leftToMax Ua.1 Vb.1) Ua.2
    letI b : M.obj (max Ua.1 Vb.1) := M.map (rightToMax Ua.1 Vb.1) Vb.2
    a • b) ?_ ?_
  · rintro ⟨U, a⟩ ⟨V₁, b₁⟩ ⟨V₂, b₂⟩ ⟨f : V₁ ⟶ V₂, rfl : b₂ = M.map _ b₁⟩
    obtain ⟨s, α, β, h₁, h₂⟩ :=
      bowtie (leftToMax U V₁) (leftToMax U V₂)
        (rightToMax U V₁) (f ≫ rightToMax U V₂)
    refine Functor.ιColimitType_eq_of_map_eq_map _ _ _ α β ?_
    simp [*, ← R.map_comp_apply, ← M.map_comp_apply, -Functor.map_comp]
  · rintro ⟨U₁, a₁⟩ ⟨U₂, a₂⟩ ⟨V, b⟩ ⟨f : U₁ ⟶ U₂, rfl : a₂ = R.map _ a₁⟩
    obtain ⟨s, α, β, h₁, h₂⟩ :=
      bowtie (leftToMax U₁ V) (f ≫ leftToMax U₂ V)
        (rightToMax U₁ V) (rightToMax U₂ V)
    refine Functor.ιColimitType_eq_of_map_eq_map _ _ _ α β ?_
    simp [*, ← R.map_comp_apply, ← M.map_comp_apply, -Functor.map_comp]

/-!
## Project-local Mathlib supplement — cover-localization iso criterion for `Scheme.Modules`

A morphism `φ : M ⟶ N` of sheaves of modules on a scheme `X` is an isomorphism iff its
restriction to each member of an open cover `𝒰` is an isomorphism.  Mathlib has the
"iso ⟺ iso on every open" criterion (`Scheme.Modules.Hom.isIso_iff_isIso_app`) and the
"restrict-to-open-immersion vs. stalk" comparison (`Scheme.Modules.restrictStalkNatIso`), but not
this *joint* cover-conservativity statement.  It is the keystone of the open-immersion
Beck–Chevalley leaf of the flat-base-change development (Stacks 02KH): it lets one verify that the
base-change comparison morphism is an isomorphism by checking it on the members of an affine cover.

The reverse (content) direction goes through the underlying presheaves of abelian groups: the
forgetful functor `Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X` reflects isomorphisms, presheaves of modules are
sheaves of abelian groups (`Scheme.Modules.isSheaf`), and isomorphy of a sheaf-of-`Ab` morphism is
detected on stalks (`TopCat.Presheaf.isIso_iff_stalkFunctor_map_iso`); the per-point reduction to a
cover member is exactly `Scheme.Modules.restrictStalkNatIso`.
-/

open AlgebraicGeometry CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Hom

/-- A morphism of sheaves of modules on a scheme is an isomorphism iff its restriction to every
member of an open cover is an isomorphism.  This is the joint cover-conservativity of the family of
restriction functors `{restrictFunctor (𝒰.f j)}`; project-local because Mathlib only packages the
single-open criterion `isIso_iff_isIso_app` and the per-leg stalk comparison `restrictStalkNatIso`,
not this assembled cover statement. -/
theorem isIso_iff_isIso_restrict
    {X : Scheme} {M N : X.Modules} (φ : M ⟶ N) (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) :
    IsIso φ ↔ ∀ j, IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (𝒰.f j)).map φ) := by
  constructor
  · -- (⟹) restriction functors preserve isomorphisms.
    intro h j
    haveI := h
    infer_instance
  · -- (⟸) the content direction.
    intro hj
    -- It suffices that the underlying presheaf morphism is an iso: `toPresheaf X` reflects isos.
    haveI key : IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).map φ) := by
      -- Present `M`, `N` as sheaves of abelian groups and `φ` as a morphism of `TopCat.Sheaf Ab`.
      set F : TopCat.Sheaf Ab X.carrier := ⟨M.presheaf, M.isSheaf⟩ with hF
      set G : TopCat.Sheaf Ab X.carrier := ⟨N.presheaf, N.isSheaf⟩ with hG
      set fS : F ⟶ G := ⟨(Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).map φ⟩ with hfS_def
      -- It suffices that `fS` be an iso: `Sheaf.forget` sends it to `(toPresheaf X).map φ`.
      suffices hfS : IsIso fS by
        haveI : IsIso fS := hfS
        exact Functor.map_isIso (TopCat.Sheaf.forget Ab X.carrier) fS
      -- Detect isomorphy of the sheaf-of-`Ab` morphism on stalks.
      rw [TopCat.Presheaf.isIso_iff_stalkFunctor_map_iso]
      intro x
      change IsIso ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab x).map ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X).map φ))
      -- Choose a cover member through `x` and a preimage point `y`.
      set j := 𝒰.idx x with hj_def
      obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := 𝒰.covers x
      rw [← hy]
      -- The restricted morphism is an iso (hyp); push it through the functors to its `y`-stalk.
      haveI hrestr := hj j
      have hstalk : IsIso ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab y).map
          ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf (𝒰.X j)).map
            ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (𝒰.f j)).map φ))) :=
        Functor.map_isIso _ _
      -- `restrictStalkNatIso` conjugates the `y`-stalk of the restriction with `φ`'s `x`-stalk.
      exact (NatIso.isIso_map_iff (Scheme.Modules.restrictStalkNatIso (𝒰.f j) y) φ).mp hstalk
    exact isIso_of_reflects_iso φ (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X)

end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Hom
